brief.headline: Push for ₹0.35/NOS on measuring cups (Premier Plastic level) and faster payment to free ₹10.19 L cash; Mars publishes no financials so qualify Manjushree Technopack as second source in parallel.

priceAsk.basis: Premier Plastic supplies the same measuring cup (MESU. CUP 30MM TRANS.PP 2.5/5/10ML) at ₹0.35/NOS today; Mars is 8.6% higher. The open market shows 28 mm PP caps typically ask ₹0.85–0.95/pc with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at volume, so our ₹0.35 cup price is already market-fair and Mars's ₹0.38 carries room to match Premier.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 days after receipt to 30 days

brief.financialLeverage: Mars Plastics publishes no financials, so we cannot see their profit, debt or cash situation. Our ₹1.24 Cr spend is meaningful for a private converter, but without their numbers we build our ask on what we pay others and on the open market. The measuring-cup gap to Premier (8.6%) is narrow and defensible. Because we lack visibility into Mars's health, we should run a parallel qualification of Manjushree Technopack (India's largest rigid-plastic converter, ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health score B 65/100) to ensure supply continuity and create real competition.

evidence.point: Premier Plastic sells us the identical measuring cup at a lower price
Closing that gap saves us this much each year
Moving payment from 45 days to 30 days unlocks working cash for our business
The open market for similar PP caps shows modest room below the typical asking band at higher volume

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms; top second-source candidate and strong leverage in this negotiation

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader for pails, containers and pharma packaging — robust, profitable alternate for bottles and closures

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: Listed moulded and blow-moulded packaging supplier with broad capability across bottles and caps

risks: Mars publishes no financials, so we fly blind on their cash position and stability — if they are fragile, a hard price squeeze could disrupt supply.
Premier Plastic at ₹0.35/NOS is already our best price; if Mars cannot match, we may need to shift more volume to Premier or bring in Manjushree, which takes time to qualify.
Our ₹1.24 Cr annual spend may not give us huge leverage if Mars has larger pharma customers — check how important we are to them before pushing hard.
Faster payment (30 days) frees our cash but only works if Mars values early settlement; without knowing their borrowing cost or cash cycle, the trade may fall flat.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to bring your measuring-cup price in line with Premier Plastic at ₹0.35 and move to 30-day payment — that saves us ₹82500 a year and frees ₹10 lakh in cash, and in return we're keen to keep Mars as a preferred partner while we expand our rigid-packaging panel.
